summary: Generates a static channel containing regularly spaced pulses, optional interpolation between pulse values, and configurable pulse width/limits.
key_concepts: Pulse CHOP generates static pulse channels over a defined interval rather than an endless time-sliced stream.
Pulse values can be interpolated between pulse locations using off, linear, ease, cosine, cubic, or connect modes.
Pulse Width turns single-sample pulses into wider step regions with sample, frame, or second units.
The optional first input supplies a start/end reference so several Pulse CHOPs can share an interval.
The optional second input supplies pulse locations, with spacing, cascade, outside-pulse, and pulse-index-unit controls.
Use LFO CHOP for continuous time-driven pulse streams and Merge CHOP when multiple pulse channels need to be combined.

key_params.name: interp
key_params.note: Off, linear, ease, cubic, and other interpolation curves

key_params.name: connect
key_params.note: Hold pulse value until the next pulse

key_params.name: clamp
key_params.note: Clamp pulse values to minimum and maximum

key_params.name: minspacing
key_params.note: Minimum spacing between pulses from the second input

key_params.name: cascade
key_params.note: Cascade pulses when spacing is enforced

key_params.name: outpulse
key_params.note: Handling for pulses outside the operator range

key_params.name: pulseunit
key_params.note: Units for pulse indices from the second input

key_params.name: separateoutchan
key_params.note: Create a separate output channel per pulse

key_params.name: nonadditives
key_params.note: Prevent pulse amplitudes from adding on the same sample

key_params.name: lastpulse
key_params.note: Place the final pulse on the final sample

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

common_gotchas: Pulse CHOP produces a static channel of a specified length; use LFO CHOP for an endless time-sliced pulse stream.
By default pulses are single-sample; Pulse Width turns them into wider steps/regions.
The optional first input supplies a start/end reference so multiple Pulse CHOPs can stretch to the same interval.
The optional second input specifies pulse sample locations; each single-sample input channel is interpreted as one pulse location.
Last Pulse at Last Sample is needed if the final sample itself must carry a pulse.
Merge multiple Pulse CHOPs when a multi-channel pulse pattern is needed.
